newsitem.title: MEXICO: TMM says to detail financing by week's end.
newsitem.headline: TMM says to detail financing by week's end.

text.p: Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) plans to explain its financing strategy for the joint approximately $1.4 billion railroad concession with Kansas City Southern Industries Inc by the weekend, a TMM spokesman told Reuters Wednesday.

"We are fine-tuning and concluding the negotiations...and I expect the scheme will be defined by the end of the week," the spokesman said, adding the company is not in a hurry to negotiate plans to pay its entire debt.

The joint company formed to purchase the Northeast Railway, called Tranportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana (TFM), will owe the government 40 percent, or $560 million, by Jan. 31 for its winning concession bid. The remaining payment is due by June 5.

TFM has not yet released financing details, to the concern of analysts who have downgraded their ratings on TMM's stock. Debt rating agencies have put the companies' bonds on credit check and a number of brokerages have advised clients that TMM stock is expected to underperform the Mexican market.
Merrill Lynch and Chase Manhattan Bank have been contracted to handle financing. TMM placed $200 million in Yankee Bonds via the New York Stock Exchange on Dec. 19.
The $1.4 billion bid was about 2.6 times that of nearest competitors, and has been called excessive by analysts.

Company officials say the concession is a strategic boon to cargo shipping between Mexico and the United States. The railway links key industial cities Mexico City and Monterrey with Gulf of Mexico ports and the U.S. border.
